scenes.title: The Invisible Force: Magnets Attract
scenes.narration: Magnets exert an invisible force, attracting or repelling certain materials without direct contact. This fundamental force is responsible for everything from holding notes on your fridge to guiding compasses, a phenomenon known since ancient times.

scenes.title: Electron Spin: The Tiny Magnets
scenes.narration: The secret to magnetism lies in electrons, which behave like tiny spinning magnets. In most materials, these spins cancel out, but in ferromagnetic substances like iron, their spins align, creating a net magnetic moment.

scenes.title: Magnetic Domains: Aligned Micro-Magnets
scenes.narration: Within ferromagnetic materials, groups of atoms form magnetic domains, where electron spins are naturally aligned. When unmagnetized, these domains point randomly, but an external field can align them, creating a powerful net magnetic field.

scenes.title: Electromagnets: Controlled Magnetism
scenes.narration: An electromagnet demonstrates how electricity and magnetism are linked: passing an electric current through a coil of wire creates a magnetic field. This field can be turned on or off, and its strength adjusted, making it vital for cranes and MRI machines.

scenes.title: Applications: Powering Our World
scenes.narration: Magnetism is fundamental to countless modern technologies. From electric motors and generators that power our homes to MRI scanners for medical diagnostics and hard drives for data storage, magnets are indispensable to our daily lives.
